A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same NEMO research work, with readable main text and complete Appendices A–E. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original NEMO evaluations across nine optimization benchmarks, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and execution examples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, supplementary analyses and execution results reported in v2.

M1.justification: The extraction, memory retrieval, solver recommendation, simulator, optimizer, MBR and self-consistency procedures in Section 3 are identical. Appendix E retains the same prompts and implementation examples.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine benchmarks, standard and curated variants, OptMATH training memory and supplementary test scenarios. Dataset descriptions and coverage in Appendix A are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains OptimAI, OptiMUS, OR-LLM-Agent, CoE, OptMATH, ORLM, LLMOPT and SIRL in the same comparisons. The Best-of-5 ACA comparator in Table 3 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, sample sizes, curation procedures, compute controls, evaluation criteria and numerical tolerances remain identical in Section 4 and Appendices A–C.

E4.justification: Component and solver ablations, simulator-versus-optimizer analysis, model and retrieval sensitivity, failure analysis and the worked execution example are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B, D and E.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent runs on BWOR and ComplexOR, with standard deviations of ±1.3% and ±2.5%, respectively. The uncertainty-reporting policy in Section 4.2 and consistency/stability reporting in Table 12 are identical.

E6.justification: All numerical results, rankings and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 reports NEMO accuracy of 90.4% on OptiBench and 65.7% on OptMATH-Bench in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning for retrieval scoring, MBR utilities, consensus selection and asymmetric validation are identical. No assumptions, proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same architectural contributions and performance claims, including first or tied-first performance on eight of nine benchmarks under at least one evaluation setting.

C2.justification: Interpretations of component contributions, curation, retrieval and model scaling are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning formulation correctness, formal verification and computational overhead.

D1.justification: Section 4.2, footnote 2 changes the Hugging Face dataset destination from AnoushkaVyas/nemo-icml2026 to c3aiia3c/nemo-icml2026, including the hyperlink target. This revises access information for released intermediate outputs; no resource-content or implementation change is documented.

R1.justification: Section 5, the reference list and comparisons with prior research are identical. No cited works or research-positioning arguments are added or removed.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v2 dated 28 May 2026 to v3 dated 17 July 2026. Apart from this metadata and the resource-address edit, the wording, terminology and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–13 retain identical content, captions, formatting and placement. Rendered-page comparison establishes no layout changes beyond the replacement text in the version stamp and dataset link.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, supporting evidence, explanations and appendices are identical. v3 is an administrative update to the dataset access address and version stamp, with no meaningful change in the paper's substantive quality. The PDFs do not establish that the changed address improves resource availability.
